title: Monopoly began as a board game warning against landlords
body: In 1904 Lizzie Magie, a follower of economist Henry George, patented The Landlord’s Game to show how owning land lets landlords grow rich from rents while tenants grow poor. She designed two sets of rules: one where players race to build monopolies, and one where everyone is rewarded as wealth is created. Homemade versions spread for decades before Charles Darrow sold a variant to Parker Brothers in 1935 as Monopoly.

slides.heading: Years after Lizzie Magie’s first patent
slides.note: Magie sold her patent to Parker Brothers for $500 in 1935; their Landlord’s Game came out in 1939

slides.prompt: Magie’s game came with a twist that Monopoly dropped. What was it?
slides.answer: A second rule set where everyone is rewarded
slides.detail: One rule set had players race to build monopolies; the other rewarded everyone as wealth was created. Charles Darrow sold a variant to Parker Brothers in 1935.
